title: Possession is sometimes ka and sometimes -ka
summary: Applied the strict ka/-ka distinction and personal suffix rules, including the explicitly accepted La-ka kelvor.

user_response.text:
Recommended App Clarification
To prevent learners from misinterpreting I ka doran as "I without torso", the app entries should be updated as follows:
Entry for Ka / -ka (Particle):
Label: Particle (Possessive / Linking)
Note: "Used between a pronoun and a noun (I ka ... or Pronoun-ka ...) to indicate possession ('my', 'our', 'your')."
Entry for Ka (Preposition):
Label: Preposition (Without)
Note: "Used before a noun when NOT preceded by a pronoun (ka shal = 'without light')."
user_response.title: Possession is sometimes ka and sometimes -ka
user_response.originalSuggestion: Explain the possessive construction and its relation to -ka; do not assume the body examples are wrong.

senses.usage: Standalone ka is exclusively without or no. Ownership uses a hyphenated possessor-ka form.
Standalone ka is exclusively without or no. Ownership uses a hyphenated possessor-ka form.
Always hyphenated to the possessor: Ilin-ka emil (our meal); La-ka kelvor (their mouth). Standalone ka means without or no.
Direct personal suffix -ian, attached after the possessed noun. My. Third-person possessor-ka is also permitted, including for body parts.
